The largest country in the world is Russia.

To understand the concept of relativity, specifically time dilation, imagine time as a river. In our everyday lives, we assume this river flows at a constant, steady pace for everyone, everywhere. However, Einstein’s theory of relativity suggests that the "flow rate" of this river can actually change depending on how fast you are moving or how strong the gravitational pull is around you.

Think of it like a rubber band. If you lay the rubber band flat on a table, it represents time passing normally for someone standing still. Now, imagine you grab one end of that rubber band and stretch it out. The rubber band itself hasn't changed in material, but it has become longer and thinner. In the analogy of relativity, when you move very fast (like on that train moving near the speed of light), you are "stretching" your experience of time relative to someone who is stationary.

For the person on the train, the rubber band feels normal; their watch ticks at its usual rhythm, and they feel no different. But to an observer standing on the platform watching the train zoom by, that stretched rubber band represents a slower flow of time. They see the person on the train moving in slow motion, as if their clock is ticking much more slowly than the clock on the platform. This isn't an illusion or a mechanical error; it is a fundamental property of the universe where time itself is flexible, not fixed.
